clinical_significance: Retrocalcaneal bursitis -- a common cause of posterior heel pain, often occurring together with (and difficult to distinguish clinically from) insertional Achilles tendinopathy or Haglund's deformity (a prominent posterosuperior calcaneal tuberosity that mechanically impinges the bursa). Distinct from the Achilles tendon substance itself, which is modeled separately in this atlas's tendon data (achilles_tendon_r) and already carries its own PRP-injection literature; this bursa is the synovial-lined space anterior to (deep to) the tendon, not the tendon.
function: A true synovial bursa occupying the space between the anteroinferior surface of the Achilles tendon and the posterosuperior surface of the calcaneus, cushioning the tendon against the bone during ankle dorsiflexion/plantarflexion. Anatomically it is a complex, V-shaped virtual cavity with fibrocartilaginous and synovial walls wrapping around the posteroinferior wedge of Kager's fat pad, rather than a simple flattened sac.

injection_approach.transducer_placement: Linear high-frequency transducer in the sagittal (longitudinal) plane over the posterior ankle just proximal to the calcaneal insertion of the Achilles tendon, with the patient prone and the foot hanging off the table end; the bursa is seen as a thin triangular anechoic/hypoechoic wedge directly deep to the tendon and superficial to the calcaneus.
injection_approach.depth_layer: Deep to the Achilles tendon and superficial to the posterosuperior calcaneal tuberosity, at the tendon-bone interface; Kager's fat pad lies immediately proximal/deep to the bursa.
injection_approach.identification_cues: A distended/inflamed bursa appears as an anechoic-to-hypoechoic triangular collection wedged between the tendon and bone; Doppler may show surrounding hyperemia in active bursitis. A prominent posterosuperior calcaneal tuberosity (Haglund's deformity) is frequently seen mechanically abutting the bursa.
structures_at_risk: Achilles tendon substance itself (avoid intratendinous placement)
injection_approach.notes: Injection is typically performed with an out-of-plane or in-plane approach from the medial or lateral side, walking the needle tip along the bone surface to enter the wedge-shaped bursal space just deep to the tendon; ultrasound guidance improves accuracy over the historical blind/landmark-based approach.
injection_approach.source: Ricci V, Chang KV, Nanka O, Ozcakar L (2024) 'Superficial retrocalcaneal bursae and nerves: From anatomy to ultrasound-guided procedures.' clinical_significance: An adventitious-type superficial bursa that develops between the skin and the posterior Achilles insertion/calcaneal prominence, typically from friction against rigid or poorly fitted footwear (e.g. a stiff heel counter) -- the mechanism behind so-called 'pump bump' irritation. Presents as a superficial, mobile, often tender swelling directly over the posterior heel, distinguishable on exam and on ultrasound from the deeper retrocalcaneal bursa by its position superficial to (rather than deep to) the Achilles tendon.
function: Reduces friction between the skin overlying the posterior calcaneus/Achilles insertion and the shoe counter or other external pressure during walking; unlike the retrocalcaneal bursa it is not obligatorily present in every individual and can be considered an adventitious bursa that forms or enlarges in response to chronic superficial friction.
